messages:
sam: hi team — moved my primary residence from ny to wa on 2025-06-15 and updated address in ADP, but my July paycheck still had NY state withholding. anyone seen this happen before? worried about state tax refunds and W-2 allocation.

lily (People Ops): hey @sam — sorry about that. moving mid-year can be messy. did you submit a state tax withholding change form (IT-2104 equivalent) or mark WA as primary in the portal?

sam: i updated home addr in profile and uploaded proof of move (lease + driver's license). i didn't explicitly fill out a new IT-2104 because we hired remote-first — assumed payroll would pick it up. paycheck snippet: "State: NEW YORK - State tax withheld: $420" for period 2025-07-10.

ravi (Payroll): @sam thanks for the details. two common causes: 1) withholding table still used NY because the employment record had NY as tax state; 2) the change was made after the July payroll cutoff. we'll audit your payroll record and run a correction if needed. can you confirm the effective move date and attach the uploaded docs to PAY-3344?

sam: move date 2025-06-15. attached in the profile and sent the docs to PAY-3344 yesterday. not urgent but want to understand W-2 impact.

steph (Tax Counsel): from a tax standpoint: WA has no state income tax, so employees who become WA residents midyear generally will have state tax withheld only for wages sourced to NY (e.g., performed work physically in NY) or for the period they were NY resident. If payroll withheld in error after residency change, we can request a state refund or process a corrective W-2 (W-2c) if needed. Also check nexus rules if you temporarily worked in another state.

ravi (Payroll): audit results: PAY-3344 shows address change submitted 2025-06-20 (after the payroll cutoff for June pay but before July). however, the tax-state field in the employment record remained NY. we'll run a supplemental payroll to credit you the state withholding erroneously taken in July and adjust YTD withholding. That will reflect as "Supplemental state refund" on your next stub. ETA: processed in 3 business days.

sam: awesome — will that change cause a W-2 correction? i.e., will 2025 W-2 show less NY wages or do we issue a W-2c after year-end?

steph (Tax Counsel): if we fix the withholding before year-end and adjust YTD totals in payroll (and no mismatch between payroll and filings), the W-2 can be issued normally showing actual wages and state withholding. If state returns have already been filed with incorrect amounts and the reconciliation requires it, we may need a W-2c. We'll monitor filings; likely no W-2c if corrected promptly.

lily (People Ops): we'll keep you posted, @sam. policy note: for future moves please submit a State Withholding Change form or update the "Tax Residency" section in Self-Service as soon as the move is effective. helps avoid these cutoffs. :memo:

payroll-bot: PAY-3344 update: payroll supplemental queued for sam. expected posting: 2025-08-01. reference PAY-3344. :gear:

sam: thanks all — really appreciate the quick turnaround. i'll watch my next stub and reach out if anything looks off. :thumbsup:
